Rule 1 satisfied: 43 passing.

**Naming evaluation (first priority)**

- `basePremiumOfType` / `insuranceSumOf` / `settleClaim` / `policyReferencedBy` — all reveal intent well.
- `INSURANCE_VALUES` — a per-type lookup, exactly parallel to `BASE_PREMIUMS`. Name fits.
- No renames warranted; the Green phase already named `basePremiumOfType` well.

**Rule 3: duplication.** The clearest remaining duplication is *conceptual*: `BASE_PREMIUMS` and `INSURANCE_VALUES` are two parallel tables keyed by the same closed set of item types, and each has its own lookup path — one that throws on an unknown type, one that silently falls back to `?? 0`. That fallback is now the only place an unknown type can pass unnoticed, and it makes the two tables drift-prone (adding a type to one and not the other compiles fine).

Let me collapse them into a single catalogue with one shared lookup.

content.text: 43 green. Let me check the typecheck too.

Typecheck clean. Refactoring is done.

## Refactor Phase Complete

**Naming evaluation (done first):** Reviewed every function name against current behaviour. `basePremiumOfType`, `insuranceSumOf`, `settleClaim`, `policyReferencedBy`, `typeGroupPremium`, `qualifiesForHalfReimbursement` all still describe what they do accurately. No renames warranted — the Green phase named `basePremiumOfType` well when it introduced the throw.

**Refactoring applied (Rule 3 — no duplication):** `BASE_PREMIUMS` and `INSURANCE_VALUES` were two parallel `Record<string, number | undefined>` tables keyed by the same closed set of item types. That's conceptual duplication: "which item types the MHPCO insures" was knowledge represented in two places. Collapsed into one `ITEM_TYPES` catalogue of `{ basePremium, insuranceValue }` with a single `termsOfType` lookup that throws, plus two thin accessors.

**The bug this closes.** `insuranceSumOf` had a `?? 0` fallback, so an unknown item type reaching the claim path contributed 0 to the insurance sum instead of raising. It didn't surface in tests because `runScenario` always quotes before it claims, and the quote path throws first — but the two tables could silently drift, and a type added to `BASE_PREMIUMS` only would have quoted fine and then computed a cap of 0. Both lookups now share one throwing path, so that whole class of divergence is structurally impossible rather than merely untested. This directly supports the "damage entry naming an item not in the policy" error case still to come.

**APP mass:**

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Table entries (constants) | 12 | 12 |
| Lookup bindings | 2 tables + 1 local | 1 table + 1 local |
| Conditionals | 2 (`if` throw + `??`) | 1 (`if` throw) |
| Invocations | 2 | 4 (two accessors delegating) |

Net roughly 22 → 20. The `??` conditional (mass 4) and the duplicate table binding are gone; two small delegating invocations (mass 2 each) were added. The mass reduction is modest — the real win is Rule 3, and the two accessors are worth their mass under Rule 2 since `insuranceValueOfType(item.type)` reads better at the call site than `termsOfType(item.type).insuranceValue`.

**Rules 2 and 4:** No change made. Names were already clear; the abstractions all earn their place (each has ≥2 callers or documents a non-obvious rule via its comment). Notably the two enchantment thresholds stay separate — `HIGH_ENCHANTMENT_LEVEL` (5, premium) and `CLAIM_HIGH_ENCHANTMENT_LEVEL` (8, claim) are unrelated rules that merely look similar, and the existing comment says so. Merging them would be false DRY.

**Tests:** 43 passing, 10 todo, `tsc --noEmit` clean.
